title: Rafic Hariri killed by Beirut truck bomb
why: 22 dead incl. ex-PM Hariri; triggers Cedar Revolution and the end of Syria's tutelage.

title: Syria completes troop withdrawal from Lebanon
why: Follows the Cedar Revolution protests; Syrian troops had been in Lebanon since the civil war.

title: Israel-Hezbollah 34-day war begins
why: About 1,191-1,300 Lebanese killed, ~1 million displaced; ended by ceasefire on 14 August.

title: Army fights Fatah al-Islam at Nahr al-Bared
why: Camp destroyed, 27,000+ Palestinians displaced; army takes control 2 September.

title: Hezbollah-led clashes seize West Beirut
why: Roughly 70-110 dead; worst internal fighting since the civil war until then.

title: Doha Agreement ends 18-month political crisis
why: Suleiman becomes president; opposition gets cabinet veto; arms question deferred.

title: Registered Syrian refugees in Lebanon pass 1 million
why: Highest per-capita refugee load in the world; strains power, water, schools, jobs.

title: Suleiman's term ends; presidency vacant 29 months
why: Parliament fails to elect a successor until October 2016.

title: Naameh landfill closes; garbage piles up in Beirut
why: Sparks the 2015 YouStink protests, the first big cross-sectarian civic movement.

title: YouStink protests peak in Beirut
why: Tear gas and water cannon; 100,000+ join by 29 August; movement fades by December.

title: Michel Aoun elected president
why: Ends 29-month vacancy via a deal with Hariri and Hezbollah; 83 votes.

title: Hariri announces resignation from Riyadh
why: Rescinded 5 December after French and Lebanese mediation.

title: CEDRE conference pledges ~$11bn for Lebanon
why: Aid tied to reforms that mostly did not happen; date and total not re-verified.

title: First parliamentary elections in nine years
why: Hezbollah and allies gain; date from memory, not re-verified in this pass.

title: Banks shut two weeks, reopen with informal capital controls
why: Dollar withdrawal limits with no law behind them; black-market rate starts to diverge.

title: WhatsApp tax sparks nationwide 17 October protests
why: Largest demonstrations since 2005; slogan 'all of them means all of them'.

title: Saad Hariri resigns as prime minister
why: Follows two weeks of protests; Diab government only formed 21 January 2020.

title: Hassan Diab designated to form government
why: Technocrat cabinet backed by Hezbollah and allies; protests continue.

title: Lebanon defaults on $1.2bn Eurobond
why: First sovereign default in the country's history.

title: Beirut port explosion kills 218
why: 2,750 t ammonium nitrate; 7,000+ injured, ~300,000 displaced; no senior official convicted.

title: Diab government resigns after port blast
why: Caretaker rule and a 13-month formation deadlock follow.

title: STL convicts Salim Ayyash for Hariri murder
why: Tribunal finds no evidence of Hezbollah leadership or direct Syrian involvement.

title: Central bank ends fuel subsidies
why: Fuel queues, then pricing in dollars; Akkar tanker blast kills 33 on 15 August.

title: Mikati forms government after 13 months
why: 24 ministers; backed by Aoun and Berri; resumes IMF talks.

title: Full 24-hour nationwide blackout
why: State electricity collapses; private generators and solar become the main supply.

title: Tayouneh clashes kill seven
why: Shooting at a Hezbollah-Amal protest against Judge Bitar; worst violence since 2008.

title: Armed bank robberies by depositors begin
why: Savers use force to withdraw frozen deposits; symbol of the banking lockout.

title: Saad Hariri suspends political life
why: Sunni leadership vacuum before the 2022 elections; he returned on 14 February 2025.

title: IMF staff-level agreement: $3bn over 46 months
why: Conditional on eight prior reforms, most of which were not delivered.

title: Parliamentary elections: Hezbollah bloc loses majority
why: LF 19 seats, FPM 17, about 13 change/independents; turnout 49.19%.

title: US-brokered maritime border deal with Israel announced
why: Line 23; Qana prospect for Lebanon, Karish for Israel; signed 27 October.

title: Aoun's term ends; presidency vacant again
why: Caretaker Mikati government; 12 failed parliamentary votes over two years.

title: Official rate devalued from 1,507 to 15,000 per dollar
why: First official devaluation in 25 years; a step toward exchange-rate unification.

title: Riad Salameh's term as central bank governor ends
why: Long-serving governor exits; date not re-verified in this pass.

title: Hezbollah opens a front against Israel
why: Follows Gaza war; low-intensity exchanges for 11 months displace tens of thousands.

title: Pager and walkie-talkie attacks hit Hezbollah
why: Explosions on 17-18 September; Israel escalates to heavy strikes from 23 September.

title: Hassan Nasrallah killed in Beirut strike
why: Hezbollah's secretary-general dies; Naim Qassem later appears as his successor.

title: Israel launches ground invasion of south Lebanon
why: War displaces over 1.2 million Lebanese at its peak.

title: FATF places Lebanon on grey list
why: Two-year action plan runs to end-2026; adds friction to transfers and banking.

title: Israel-Lebanon ceasefire takes effect
why: 60 days for phased Israeli withdrawal; five-nation monitoring panel; army to deploy 5,000 troops.

title: Assad regime falls in Syria
why: Assad flees to Russia; Syrian refugees begin returning from Lebanon; border dynamics shift.

title: Joseph Aoun elected president
why: 99 votes in round two after Hezbollah and Amal blocs shift; ends two-year vacuum.

title: Nawaf Salam named prime minister
why: Former ICJ president; cabinet inaugurated 8 February, wins confidence 26 February (95 votes).

title: Israel keeps five border positions after deadline
why: Withdrawal deadline extended from 26 January to 18 February; five points retained.

title: Nasrallah funeral held in Beirut
why: Held nearly five months after his killing; mass turnout.

title: World Bank puts reconstruction needs at $11bn
why: Physical damage $6.8bn, economic losses $7.2bn for 2023-24 war.

title: Rodolphe Haykal appointed army commander
why: Later leads the state weapons-monopoly plan.

title: Karim Souaid appointed central bank governor
why: Replaces the interim leadership at the central bank; part of the 2025 reform push.

title: Parliament amends bank secrecy law
why: Ten-year lookback for regulators, judiciary and anti-corruption body; IMF prerequisite.

title: Municipal elections begin
why: First local vote since 2016; run in stages across governorates through May.

title: EU adds Lebanon to high-risk money-laundering list
why: Banks face extra checks on Lebanese flows.

title: Parliament passes bank resolution law
why: Framework to liquidate or restructure failing banks; later amended.

title: Cabinet tasks army with state monopoly on arms
why: Shia ministers walk out; 7 August cabinet endorses US (Barrack) paper's objectives.

title: UN Security Council ends UNIFIL mandate at end-2026
why: Peacekeeping presence to wind down after 47 years.

title: Cabinet accepts five-phase army disarmament roadmap
why: Phase one south of Litani; Shia ministers walk out again.

title: Israel kills Hezbollah chief of staff Tabatabai in Beirut
why: Five dead; first Beirut strike of this scale since the ceasefire.

title: Pope Leo XIV visits Lebanon
why: Three-day first trip abroad; prays at the Beirut port blast site on 2 December.

title: First direct Lebanon-Israel talks since 1983
why: Held at UNIFIL headquarters, Naqoura, under the ceasefire mechanism.

title: Cabinet approves financial gap draft law
why: 13-9 vote; deposits under $100,000 repaid over four years; gap put at $80-83bn.

title: Army says phase one south of Litani complete
why: Israel calls it insufficient; sources admit Hezbollah redeployed rather than left.

title: Block 8 gas deal signed with TotalEnergies, Eni, QatarEnergy
why: Development agreement for offshore Block 8.

title: IMF says it cannot endorse gap law as drafted
why: Salam reports IMF wants changes to deposit-recovery draft.

title: Qatar announces $430m energy sector package
why: Aimed at electricity supply.

title: US and Israel strike Iran; regional war begins
why: Khamenei's death confirmed 1 March; sets off Hezbollah's entry.

title: Hezbollah fires on Israel; Israel strikes Beirut
why: First Hezbollah fire since November 2024; start of the 2026 Lebanon war.

title: Cabinet bans Hezbollah military activity
why: Salam: war and peace belong to the state; Iran's IRGC also barred; some sources date it 2 March. (corrected from 2026-03-05)

title: Parliament extends its term by two years
why: Vote 76-41, 4 abstentions; May 2026 elections postponed, now due 2028.

title: Israel begins ground offensive in south Lebanon
why: Aim declared 24 March: control up to the Litani; Litani bridges destroyed.

title: Lebanon expels Iran's ambassador
why: Follows 5 March IRGC ban and Iranian visa requirement.

title: 'Black Wednesday': over 100 strikes in 10 minutes
why: At least 303 killed per Lebanon's health ministry; last main southern bridge damaged.

title: First direct Israel-Lebanon talks in Washington
why: Rubio hosts ambassadors; first such bilateral engagement since 1993.

title: Ten-day ceasefire takes effect
why: 5 pm EDT on 16 April is midnight in Beirut; extended 23 April and 15 May.

title: Radwan Force commander killed in Beirut strike
why: Strikes continue under the truce; toll passes 3,000 by 18 May.

title: US announces 45-day ceasefire extension
why: Follows April three-week extension; strikes continue in Nabatieh area.

title: Israel seizes Beaufort Castle
why: Israeli forces hold 570-600 km2 of southern Lebanon by later estimates.

title: Israel-Lebanon renewal creates 'pilot zones'
why: Hezbollah rejects it 4 June, demanding full withdrawal.

title: US-Iran Islamabad memorandum covers Lebanon front
why: Israel says its forces stay in Lebanon; Trump announces truce 19 June.

title: Trump announces Israel-Hezbollah truce
why: Brokered with Qatar and Iran involvement; came into force at 4 pm local.

title: Rubio announces Israel-Lebanon peace framework
why: Includes full Hezbollah disarmament; Hezbollah rejects it.

title: Israel hands buffer-zone sections to Lebanese control
why: Army deploys in Zawtar al-Gharbiyeh 21 July; direct US flights ordered.

title: New Israel-Lebanon talks open in Rome
why: Israel resumes strikes 5 August; Hezbollah urges Beirut to halt talks.

title: Lebanon and Israel agree on disarmament verifier countries
why: Reported by Times of Israel citing an official; details not fetched.

title: Parliament abolishes death penalty
why: Described as an Arab world first; amnesty law passed 12 August.

title: Parliament passes amended bank restructuring law
why: IMF calls it a major step; changes central bank governance rules.

title: World Bank forecasts 6.4% contraction
why: Projection for war-hit economy in 2026.

title: Rubio hosts Salam as talks stall
why: Israel wants disarmament first, Lebanon wants withdrawal first; Israeli strikes continue.

title: Jaber hopes for new IMF staff-level agreement
why: Gap law still unpassed; one source says within days, another by year-end.
